allFindings.evidence: Forgetting `.dispose()` leaks the observer forever (observers set, MutableState.kt:34; GUIDE.md:261-262 'observers held forever are a memory leak' and pitfalls row GUIDE.md:1004). Mitigations that DO exist: holdfast-compose collectAsState/rememberDisposable auto-dispose (ComposeBindings.kt:33-63), asFlow disposes on collection cancel (StateFlows.kt:52-57), CompositeDisposable pattern shown (GUIDE.md:842-853). But there is no runtime detection, and the one introspection hook — observerCount — is @StoreInternalApi at RequiresOptIn.Level.ERROR with KDoc saying 'Application code must never read this' (MutableState.kt:48-50, 261-266), so an app team cannot even write the leak-canary test the library's own modules use.
allFindings.recommendation: Expose a supported `State<T>.observerCount` (or `Store.debugObserverCounts(): Map<String, Int>`) in :holdfast-testing so apps can assert zero leaked subscriptions in tests, and reference it from the GUIDE pitfalls row.

allFindings.title: GUIDE middleware-ordering paragraph contradicts the code and the Store/Middleware KDoc — affects which middleware observes errors
allFindings.evidence: GUIDE.md:308-309: 'middlewares(A, B) runs A's started hook first, then B's…'. Code: Store.kt:405-413 folds the chain so the LAST-registered middleware is outermost — B's started fires FIRST — exactly as Store.kt:303-315 and Middleware.kt:15-20 document ('for an onTransactionError handler to see exceptions thrown by another middleware, it must be listed AFTER that middleware'), and as SuspendAction.kt:97 implements (reversed iteration). A user following the GUIDE will place their error-logging middleware on the wrong end and never see validation errors.
allFindings.recommendation: Fix GUIDE.md:308-309 to state last-registered = outermost (started first, completed/error last) and repeat the practical rule: register logging/audit middleware LAST.

allFindings.title: GUIDE claims action 'never throws' but the disposed-store path throws synchronously
allFindings.evidence: GUIDE.md:201 'It never throws — exceptions are captured into Error.' vs Store.kt:355 checkNotDisposed() throwing IllegalStateException('store disposed') BEFORE the transaction machinery, verified by StoreDisposeTest.kt:42-52. The exception is intentional (and good — louder than a buried Error), but the absolute 'never' in the GUIDE will mislead someone writing a wrapper that assumes action is total.
allFindings.recommendation: Amend to 'never throws for failures inside the body or commit; it does throw IllegalStateException if the store is disposed' — one sentence.

allFindings.title: Store.defaultScope double-set message is good but omits where the first assignment happened
allFindings.evidence: Store.kt:711-717: `check(customDefaultScope.compareAndSet(null, value)) { "Store.defaultScope is settable-once; it has already been assigned." }` — clear, states the rule and the fact. In a multi-module app (or app + library both initializing Holdfast), the dev's next question is 'assigned by WHOM?' and the error cannot answer it.
allFindings.recommendation: In debug builds, capture a Throwable() stack (or at least the thread name/time) at first assignment and append it to the failure message; alternatively document the 'who owns app init' convention in the GUIDE (defaultScope currently appears in no GUIDE section at all — grep found zero hits).

allFindings.title: context(CoroutineScope) overloads silently hijack the ambient coroutine scope; KDoc resolution claim is contradicted by the project's own tests
allFindings.evidence: StateFlows.kt:115-118 declares `context(scope: CoroutineScope) fun State<T>.asStateFlow(...)` alongside the default-param form at StateFlows.kt:90-93. The KDoc at StateFlows.kt:106-109 claims 'outside any context(...) block, the call site resolves to the default-param form and picks up store.scope'. The library's own test comments contradict this: AsStateFlowContextParamTest.kt:49-56 ('K2 implicit-receiver resolution inside runBlocking { } can prefer the context-param overload (the runBlocking scope is in the implicit chain)') and BridgeFactoryContextParamTest.kt:28-30 say the same for the bridge factories (SuspendingBridge.kt:116-120, 179-183). Any call inside `launch {}`, `runBlocking {}`, `coroutineScope {}`, a `fun CoroutineScope.x()` helper, or Compose `LaunchedEffect {}` has an implicit CoroutineScope receiver, so K2 fills the context parameter from it. Consequence: `viewModelScope.launch { cached = store.count.asStateFlow() }` scopes the stateIn sharing job to the transient launch coroutine — when it completes, the StateFlow goes silently dead (never updates again), with zero compiler or runtime signal. Same silent capture applies to `SuspendingKvStore.bridge`/`suspendingBridge` drainer coroutines.
allFindings.recommendation: Remove the context-parameter overloads (or rename them, e.g. `asStateFlowInContext()`) so the implicit-receiver chain can never silently outcompete the documented default. If kept, (a) fix the KDoc on all three pairs to state the truth — any enclosing coroutine body WILL capture its scope — and (b) add a prominent footgun warning with the dead-StateFlow example. A test asserting the dangerous resolution (rather than a comment calling it 'fragile') would lock the behavior down.

allFindings.title: No user-facing threading/scoping documentation: scope chain, bindToScope, defaultScope, and dispose are absent from GUIDE.md, both READMEs, and the API reference
allFindings.evidence: GUIDE.md (billed as 'Complete Guide', ~1700 lines) contains zero occurrences of `bindToScope`, `defaultScope`, `Store.scope`, `dispose()`/`isDisposed` (grep verified). The §13 API-reference Store table (GUIDE.md:1012-1024) omits `scope`, `bindToScope`, `dispose`, `isDisposed`, `defaultScope`. §10 'Concurrency Model' (GUIDE.md:858-908) covers locks and transactions but never mentions coroutine scopes. holdfast/README.md:126-137 'Concurrency model' likewise. The 4-level resolution chain exists only in Store.kt:71-84 KDoc. A user asking 'which scope does my asStateFlow() collect on with nothing set?' must reverse-engineer KDoc fragments across two modules to learn the answer (lazy process-global SupervisorJob+Dispatchers.Default scope, Store.kt:688-690, never cancelled — which silently leaks an Eagerly-started stateIn forever).
allFindings.recommendation: Add a 'Threading & Scopes' section to GUIDE.md covering: the 4-level resolution chain with a worked example per level; what the implicit process default is and that it is never cancelled (so SharingStarted.Eagerly on it leaks); bindToScope vs subclass override precedence; dispose() semantics and its scope asymmetry; and which thread observers fire on. Add `scope`/`bindToScope`/`dispose`/`isDisposed`/`defaultScope` rows to the §13 API table.

allFindings.title: Observers fire synchronously on the committing thread while the transaction lock is held — undocumented at effect, and GUIDE actively claims the opposite
allFindings.evidence: Commit fanout runs inside `transactionLock.withLock` (Store.kt:369-403: `txn.commit()` at line 387 is inside the lock), and `notifyObservers` holds `observersLock` while invoking every observer (MutableState.kt:165-176). StoreLock waiters busy-spin via `threadYield()` (StoreLock.kt:21-23, JVM Threading.kt: `Thread.yield()`), so a slow `effect {}` handler stalls every other thread's `action {}` in a CPU-burning spin, not a parked wait. Effect.kt:1-31 KDoc says nothing about which thread the handler runs on or that it runs under the store's locks. Worse, GUIDE.md:868 states 'Snapshot then fire — observer callback NOT under lock', which is false on two counts (observersLock held during fanout; transactionLock held for the whole commit). A user porting an MVI side-effect (logging, analytics, even a blocking DB write) into `effect {}` has no warning they are serializing their entire store behind it.
allFindings.recommendation: Fix the GUIDE.md:868 table row. Add to the `effect` KDoc (Effect.kt) and GUIDE §10: 'handlers run synchronously on the committing thread while the store's transaction lock is held; keep them fast and non-blocking; never call another store's action from a handler; use asFlow()/asStateFlow() to move work to a coroutine.' Consider documenting that contending actions busy-spin rather than park, since that turns 'slow observer' into 'CPU burn' on mobile.

allFindings.title: Blocking action{} inside (or concurrent with) suspendAction self-deadlocks as a silent infinite busy-spin; guaranteed browser freeze on wasmJs
allFindings.area: coroutines interop / mixing blocking and suspending
allFindings.evidence: `action` brackets through `serializer.blockingAcquire()` (Store.kt:359-365), which spins `while (!mutex.tryLock(SPIN_OWNER)) threadYield()` (AsyncSerializer.kt:23-28). If a user calls a helper that uses blocking `action {}` from inside a `suspendAction {}` body, the mutex is held by their own coroutine → infinite spin at 100% CPU, no exception, no diagnostic. On wasmJs, `threadYield()` is a no-op (Threading.wasmJs.kt:5-7) and the event loop is blocked by the spin, so ANY blocking `action {}` while a `suspendAction` is suspended hard-freezes the tab — the suspended coroutine can never resume to release the mutex. SuspendAtomic.kt:56-60 documents the analogous limitation for `suspendAtomic` (KDoc only), but SuspendAction.kt:27-31 and GUIDE.md:1283-1287 only say blocking action 'will block until the in-flight suspendAction completes' — never warning about the nested-call case, the busy-spin (ANR risk if the blocked caller is the main thread), or the single-threaded-platform freeze.
allFindings.recommendation: Detect the nested case and throw: in `action`, if `suspendingOwner != null` and the current coroutine/thread is the suspendAction owner, fail fast with 'cannot call blocking action inside suspendAction; use mutate or a nested suspendAction'. Document the mixing rules in one place (GUIDE §14.8 + SuspendAction KDoc): blocking-waits-spinning, main-thread ANR caveat, and an explicit 'on wasmJs use suspendAction exclusively' rule. Consider making blockingAcquire on wasmJs throw immediately instead of freezing.

allFindings.title: Store.defaultScope settable-once-per-process breaks users' test suites; holdfast-testing offers no escape
allFindings.evidence: Store.kt:711-717: second assignment throws IllegalStateException via CAS. The library's own tests had to be contorted around this — StoreScopeTest.kt:16-18: 'Tests here are written to be order-independent: whichever test first sets defaultScope wins'. A user who writes `@BeforeTest { Store.defaultScope = TestScope(...) }` gets a throw on every test after the first in the same JVM/process, with shared mutable state leaking across tests if the first assignment wins. holdfast-testing (StoreTestScope.kt, StoreTest.kt) never touches defaultScope/bindToScope, so the official testing harness gives no help; the workaround (per-store `bindToScope`, which IS rebindable, Store.kt:87-102) is not suggested anywhere in testing docs or the defaultScope KDoc.
allFindings.recommendation: Either (a) ship a `@StoreTestApi resetDefaultScopeForTesting()` in holdfast-testing and have `holdfastTest { }` auto-bind tracked stores to the TestScope, or (b) document the canonical pattern prominently on the defaultScope KDoc and GUIDE: 'never assign defaultScope in tests; use store.bindToScope(testScope) per test'. The KDoc currently shows only the app-init pattern (Store.kt:701-705).

allFindings.title: holdfast-coroutines README and GUIDE §14.8 document a stale API surface — wrong asStateFlow signature, removed asEagerStateFlow, missing suspendAction in module README, stale pre-rename class names
allFindings.evidence: holdfast-coroutines/README.md:11-14 shows `asStateFlow(scope: CoroutineScope, ...)` with scope required — actual signature defaults it to `owningScope` (StateFlows.kt:90-93); the README never mentions suspendAction/suspendDerived/suspendAtomic/SuspendingBridge/context overloads even though the root README.md:46 advertises suspendAction as the module's headline; it uses pre-rename class names `CounterHoldfast`/`AccountHoldfast` (lines 36, 47) inconsistent with the Store* rename. GUIDE.md:1275 still lists `fun State<T>.asEagerStateFlow(): EagerStateFlow<T>` which StateFlows.kt:88 KDoc describes as 'the removed asEagerStateFlow()'. GUIDE.md:1274 also shows the old required-scope signature. A new adopter following the module README will pass scopes explicitly everywhere and never learn the store-scope default exists; one who copies `asEagerStateFlow()` gets a compile error against a 'Complete Guide'.
allFindings.recommendation: Regenerate both docs against the current surface: default-param asStateFlow, the context overloads (with the capture warning from the blocker finding), suspendAction/suspendDerived/suspendAtomic, and delete asEagerStateFlow. Add an apiCheck-style CI step or doc test that compiles GUIDE/README snippets to keep them honest.

allFindings.title: Inconsistent ambient-scope defaults across factories: asStateFlow uses owning store's scope, bridge factories use process defaultScope
allFindings.evidence: StateFlows.kt:90-93 defaults `scope = owningScope` (resolves through the store's 4-level chain). SuspendingBridge.kt:94 and :158 default `scope: CoroutineScope = Store.defaultScope` (skipping the store chain entirely — bindToScope on a store has no effect on bridges attached to its states). Plus the context-parameter overloads as a third resolution rule. Three different 'which scope did I get?' answers for sibling APIs in the same module.
allFindings.recommendation: Document the difference side by side in the module README ('flows follow the store's scope; bridges follow the process default unless passed explicitly — bind the bridge scope yourself if you bound the store'). Longer term, consider a `bridge(key, codec)` overload resolved at attach time from the owning store's scope so the chain applies uniformly.

allFindings.title: bindToScope silently no-ops when a subclass overrides scope; chain level numbering forces KDoc cross-referencing
allFindings.evidence: Store.kt:83-84: `open val scope get() = boundScope ?: defaultScope` — a subclass `override val scope` discards `boundScope` entirely, so a consumer calling `thirdPartyStore.bindToScope(myScope)` gets no error and no effect. It IS documented (Store.kt:88-89, 77-79), but only in KDoc the binder may never read; there is no runtime signal. The chain is also described twice with level numbers ('resolution level 3', Store.kt:60-63, 87) requiring cross-referencing to decode.
allFindings.recommendation: Cheap improvement: have `bindToScope` detect that `this::scope` is overridden (e.g. compare `scope` identity before/after binding) and log via uncaughtObserverHandler-style hook, or at minimum return a Boolean 'binding is effective'. In docs, present the chain once as a 4-row table in GUIDE with 'who wins' examples rather than KDoc level numbers.

allFindings.title: suspendDerived is unusable on wasmJs (runBlocking seed throws) and blocks the calling thread elsewhere — platform limitation absent from GUIDE/README
allFindings.evidence: SuspendDerived.kt:80 seeds the initial value via `runBlockingForInitialSeed`; the wasmJs actual (holdfast-coroutines/src/wasmJsMain/.../RunBlocking.kt:3-8) throws UnsupportedOperationException at first call. The exception message is good (names the cause and suggests `store.suspendAction { ... }`), but the KDoc (SuspendDerived.kt:55-59) mentions only 'the caller blocks' and neither GUIDE nor README mentions that a commonMain API is a guaranteed runtime throw on one supported target. The 'caller blocks on long initial compute' is also an easy main-thread jank trap on Android.
allFindings.recommendation: Add a 'Platform notes' block to suspendDerived's KDoc and GUIDE: wasmJs → throws at construction (with the workaround); JVM/iOS → initial compute blocks the constructing thread, keep it cheap or construct off-main. Consider an `initial: T` overload that skips the runBlocking seed entirely — it removes both problems.

allFindings.title: dispose()/scope-cancellation asymmetry is well documented in KDoc but invisible in the guides
allFindings.evidence: Store.kt:126-134 documents the asymmetry crisply ('cancelling the bound scope is a soft-pause...; dispose() is terminal') and bindToScope's KDoc (Store.kt:96-98) covers the non-cancellation contract. But GUIDE.md's pitfalls table (§12) and API reference never mention dispose() at all, so a ViewModel author deciding between `onCleared { store.dispose() }` and `onCleared { scope.cancel() }` finds guidance only by reading base-class source.
allFindings.recommendation: Add a GUIDE lifecycle subsection with the ViewModel teardown recipe: cancel the scope you own AND dispose the store you own; note that cancelled-bound-scope stores silently fall back to defaultScope for new async work (the 'soft-pause' surprise).

allFindings.title: Install instructions and Maven Central badge point at artifacts that do not exist on Maven Central
allFindings.evidence: README.md:4 (Maven Central badge for com.vynatix/holdfast), README.md:52-68 (Install section: mavenCentral() + implementation("com.vynatix:holdfast:0.1.0")), holdfast/CHANGELOG.md:13 ('First public release on Maven Central as com.vynatix:holdfast'). Live check: https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/com/vynatix/holdfast/ returns HTTP 404 and central.sonatype.com search for g:com.vynatix returns numFound:0. Publish version default '0.1.0' is set in buildSrc/src/main/kotlin/holdfast.publish.gradle.kts:21 but nothing is published.
allFindings.recommendation: Either publish 0.1.0 before merging these docs, or change the Install section to publishToMavenLocal/snapshot instructions and remove/soften the badge and the changelog 'released on Maven Central' claim until the artifacts resolve. A new user's literal first step (Gradle sync) currently fails.

allFindings.title: Test DSL documented as `holdfastTest { }` but the real entry point is `vaultTest` (pre-rename residue in the public API)
allFindings.evidence: README.md:48 and holdfast/README.md:98 document `holdfastTest { }`. Actual function: holdfast-testing/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/vynatix/holdfast/testing/StoreTest.kt:32 `fun vaultTest(timeout..., body...)`; confirmed in holdfast-testing/api/jvm dump line 176-179 (StoreTestKt.vaultTest). The KDoc sample at StoreTest.kt:15-16 even uses `vaultTest { val ctr = track(CountVault()) }` — another stale class name. Related public-API residue: MutableState.kt:27 public `owningVault: Store<*>`, EventfulSupport.kt:88 `bindVault(store)` with error text 'EventfulSupport.bindVault must be called...' (EventfulSupport.kt:107-108).
allFindings.recommendation: Rename `vaultTest` → `storeTest` (or `holdfastTest` to match docs), `bindVault` → `bindStore`, `owningVault` → `owningStore`, and fix the StoreTest.kt KDoc sample. Until the rename lands, fix README.md:48 and holdfast/README.md:98 to say `vaultTest`. Users searching docs for the documented name find nothing; users who find vaultTest hit branding that matches nothing else in the library.

allFindings.title: holdfast-compose README example does not compile (delegated local shadows the state property)
allFindings.evidence: holdfast-compose/README.md:22-33: `val count by holdfast.collectAsState(holdfast.count)` creates a local `count: Int`; the button then calls `holdfast.action { count update { it + 1 } }` — inside the action lambda the local Int shadows the store's `count: State<Int>`, and `update` (Store.kt:520, member-extension on State<T>) cannot apply to Int → compile error. Also `CounterHoldfast` (line 23) and `AccountHoldfast` (line 40) are class names that exist nowhere.
allFindings.recommendation: Rename the local (`val countValue by ...`) or qualify inside the action (`this.count update { it + 1 }`), use Store* class names, and compile-check the snippet. This shadowing trap is also worth a dedicated pitfall entry in GUIDE §12 since every Compose user will hit it.

allFindings.title: Stale pre-rename class names (CounterHoldfast / AccountHoldfast / UserHoldfast) survive in four docs
allFindings.evidence: holdfast-coroutines/README.md:36 (`CounterHoldfast()`), :47 (`AccountHoldfast`); holdfast-compose/README.md:23,40; holdfast-hallmark-coroutines/README.md:29 (`UserHoldfast`); GUIDE.md:643-644 (`Middleware<AccountHoldfast>`); GUIDE.md:1331 mixes both in one signature: `fun AccountStore.transferTo(other: AccountHoldfast, cents: Long)`. Repo convention after the rename commits (539820d, 1dc226a) is Store* names (CounterStore etc. in README.md:16, GUIDE.md:78).
allFindings.recommendation: Mechanical sweep: replace *Holdfast class names with *Store across all .md files (grep 'Holdfast()' and '[A-Z][a-z]*Holdfast'). Copy-paste users get unresolved references and learn the library's own docs aren't trustworthy.

allFindings.title: 'No coroutines dependency in core' claim is false — core exposes kotlinx-coroutines as an api() dependency and in public types
allFindings.evidence: holdfast/README.md:12 ('No coroutines dependency in core'), holdfast/README.md:171-173 ('no required dependencies beyond kotlin-stdlib + kotlinx-atomicfu'), GUIDE.md:5-6 ('no coroutine dependency in its API'). Contradicted by holdfast/build.gradle.kts:49 `api(libs.kotlinx.coroutines.core)` and by public API types: Store.getScope(): CoroutineScope, Store.bindToScope(CoroutineScope), Store.Companion.defaultScope, EventfulStore events: SharedFlow (holdfast/api/jvm/holdfast.api lines 25-46, 115-155).
allFindings.recommendation: Rewrite the positioning claim: 'core depends on kotlinx-coroutines-core (api) for store scope and events; no Compose/Android/iOS framework deps.' If zero-coroutines-core is a real design goal, that is a code change, not a doc fix — but right now the doc promises a dependency profile the artifact does not have, which matters to exactly the audience (KMP library authors) the claim targets.

allFindings.title: GUIDE documents removed API `asEagerStateFlow` / `EagerStateFlow`
allFindings.evidence: GUIDE.md:1275 `fun <T : Any> State<T>.asEagerStateFlow(): EagerStateFlow<T>`. Not present in holdfast-coroutines/api/jvm/holdfast-coroutines.api (StateFlowsKt has only asFlow/asStateFlow/awaitValue/first). holdfast-coroutines/CHANGELOG.md:59 documents the migration away from it ('state.asEagerStateFlow().also { it.dispose() } →').

allFindings.title: GUIDE claims same-value commits are deduped by default; code dedupes only with opt-in `distinct = true`
allFindings.evidence: GUIDE.md:247-249 (§4.4: 'Same-value commits do not re-fire — see §6') and GUIDE.md:424 (§6 table row 'no fire — dedup' / 'no publish — dedup') describe dedup as the default. Actual: Store.kt:427-434 (`distinct: Boolean = false`, KDoc: 'Pass [distinct] = true to skip observer fanout...') and MutableState.kt:127 `val same = distinct && currentValue == processedValue` — with default false, same-value commits DO re-fire observers and re-publish bridges. GUIDE §13 line 1015 states it correctly ('distinct=true opts into same-value commit dedup'), contradicting §4.4/§6 in the same document.
allFindings.recommendation: Fix §4.4 and the §6 visibility table to state the default (same-value commit fires) and show `state(distinct = true)` as the opt-in. This is a behavioral footgun: users will skip equality guards in effects because the guide promised dedup, then get duplicate UI updates/persistence writes.

allFindings.title: GUIDE contradicts itself on middleware ordering (§4.6 says first-arg-outermost; §13/§14.6/source say last-arg-outermost)
allFindings.evidence: GUIDE.md:308-311 (§4.6): 'Middleware composes left-to-right: middlewares(A, B) runs A's started hook first, then B's...'. Contradicted by GUIDE.md:1018 (§13: 'LAST argument is outermost'), GUIDE.md:1239-1242 (§14.6 same), and source of truth Store.kt:304-306 KDoc + Store.kt:409 fold ('the LAST argument is the outermost middleware (its onTransactionStarted runs first)'). So §4.6 — the section beginners read — is the wrong one.
allFindings.recommendation: Correct §4.6 to: `middlewares(A, B)` runs B's started hook first (B outermost), then A's, then the body, then A's completed, then B's. Add one worked log-output example so ordering is unambiguous; ordering bugs in logging/validation middleware are silent.

allFindings.title: Core README presents `transaction(on = store) { }` as a core transaction primitive; it is a test-only utility in holdfast-testing
allFindings.evidence: holdfast/README.md:54: 'Transactions (`action { … }` or `transaction(on = store) { … }`) are atomic units of mutation.' No such function in core (grep of holdfast/src/commonMain finds nothing; holdfast.api has no top-level transaction fn). It exists in holdfast-testing/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/vynatix/holdfast/testing/concurrency/OpenTransaction.kt (:181 KDoc 'val open = transaction(on = ctr) { count mutate 999 } // pending, not committed') — and it deliberately leaves the transaction OPEN, the opposite of what the README sentence implies.
allFindings.recommendation: Remove `transaction(on = store)` from holdfast/README.md:54 (core has exactly one entry point: action / suspendAction). Document transaction(on=) only in testing docs, clearly labeled as 'open an uncommitted transaction for visibility tests'.

allFindings.title: GUIDE §14.11 and hallmark-coroutines README use pre-rename module coordinates (com.vynatix:validation, :validation-coroutines, holdfast-validation)
allFindings.evidence: GUIDE.md:1363-1378 (module table lists `com.vynatix:validation`, `com.vynatix:validation-coroutines`; prose ':validation is a standalone KMP refinement-types library'), GUIDE.md:1539 ('Holdfast integration (holdfast-validation)'), GUIDE.md:1576, GUIDE.md:1606 ('holdfast-validation-coroutines'); holdfast-hallmark-coroutines/README.md:3 ('Bridges :validation-coroutines'). allFindings.recommendation: Search-and-replace validation→hallmark coordinates throughout GUIDE §14.11 and the hallmark-coroutines README, and state explicitly that Hallmark core lives in a separate repo. Right now a reader cannot construct a working dependency line for the validation feature from the guide.

allFindings.title: Eight broken links to ../MIGRATING.md plus a broken validation/KONFORM-MIGRATION.md link

allFindings.title: Lifecycle and events surface (dispose/bindToScope/scope/defaultScope/Eventful) is completely undocumented outside the changelog
allFindings.evidence: Public API (holdfast/api/jvm/holdfast.api lines 25-46, 115-165): Eventful, EventfulStore, EventfulSupport, Store.dispose(), isDisposed, bindToScope(CoroutineScope), scope, Store.Companion.defaultScope, postCommit. allFindings.title: Module documentation coverage is inconsistent: holdfast-testing and holdfast-hallmark have no README; holdfast-coroutines README documents a fraction of its surface

allFindings.title: GUIDE section 14 is organized around internal version numbers (1.0/1.1/2.0/0.3.0) that no published artifact ever had

allFindings.title: GUIDE §13 API reference drift: documents non-public Transaction.parent, misplaces effect, omits new Store members; §2 file layout is stale

allFindings.title: 'Rejected at compile time' wording for cross-store ownership is wrong (it is a runtime check)
allFindings.evidence: holdfast/README.md:79: 'foreign-store states are rejected at compile time of the call (runtime ownership check at O(1))' — self-contradictory; GUIDE.md:961-972 (§11.4) and GUIDE.md:1001 show the rejection is a runtime TransactionResult.Error / IllegalStateException.

allFindings.title: No doc answers 'which modules do I need?' or 'how do I migrate from StateFlow/ViewModel?'; the only Compose guidance hand-rolls a bridge
allFindings.evidence: README.md:41-50 module table describes roles but no decision guidance (e.g. testing vs hallmark vs coroutines dependencies between them); GUIDE §7 decision charts (GUIDE.md:439-565) cover only in-core choices. Add a GUIDE section: 'Coming from MutableStateFlow' (cell-by-cell mapping: MutableStateFlow.value= → mutate, combine → derived, collectAsState → compose module). Rewrite §9.5 to use the shipped adapters and demote the hand-rolled bridge to an 'under the hood' note.

allFindings.title: Terminology drift: holdfast/store/vault used interchangeably for the same concept
allFindings.evidence: Class is `Store` but docs say 'cross-holdfast atomic' (README.md:45), 'foreign-holdfast state' (GUIDE.md:1001), variables named `holdfast` (GUIDE.md:135 `val holdfast = TodoStore()`), 'Calling on an already-bound vault rebinds' (holdfast/CHANGELOG.md:55), `atomic(vararg holdfasts)` heading (GUIDE.md:1166) vs `atomic(vararg stores)` signature (GUIDE.md:1169).

allFindings.title: Root README dependency snippet omits the hallmark artifacts and shows non-KMP dependency placement
allFindings.evidence: README.md:62-68 lists holdfast, -coroutines, -compose, -testing but not holdfast-hallmark / holdfast-hallmark-coroutines (rows exist in the table at README.md:49-50). allFindings.title: External companion link (vynatix/banking-demo) and hallmark repo links are unverifiable from the docs alone
allFindings.evidence: holdfast/README.md:179 promises '[vynatix/banking-demo](https://github.com/vynatix/banking-demo) ... exercising every public API ... plus 186 feature-coverage tests'; README.md:79 links github.com/vynatix/hallmark. allFindings.evidence: Root README.md:48 documents the module as "Testing harness — `holdfastTest { }`, `StoreHandle`, timeline matchers"; holdfast/README.md:98 repeats "**`holdfastTest { }`** scope with auto-tracking". allFindings.evidence: The library is Holdfast, the central class is `Store` (recent rename commits 539820d/b0c6cb0), yet the harness entry point is `vaultTest` (StoreTest.kt:32) — typing "store" or "holdfast" in IDE completion finds nothing. 43 occurrences of "vault" remain in commonMain KDoc/samples: `TimelineMatcher.vaultRef` (TimelineMatcher.kt:53), sample classes `CountVault` (StoreTest.kt:16), `MyVault` (StoreAutoRegistration.kt:17, Awaiting.kt:37), `SettingsVault` (FakeKvStore.kt:23, BridgeView.kt:36), "do these vaults look the same?" (StateMatchers.kt:112). allFindings.title: Core's member `Store.action` silently shadows the scope's auto-tracking `action {}` — recorder never installs AND errors escape the pending-error guard
allFindings.evidence: StoreAutoRegistration.kt:47-63 documents the caveat: `v.action { }` always resolves to the member `Store.action` (holdfast/src/.../Store.kt:354), so it never auto-registers. Consequences are silent: (1) timeline is empty unless something else registered first — the harness's OWN tests need a warm-up wart with an explanatory comment, e.g. AutoRegistrationTest.kt:56 `v.read { } // installs the recorder via auto-registration` repeated in 8 tests; (2) even after registration, `v.action {}` bypasses `StoreHandle.action`, so `lastResult` is not fed (AutoRegistrationTest.kt:258-261: "Store.action (the member, the shadowing function) does not feed the handle's lastResult slot") and — worse — a `TransactionResult.Error` returned from `v.action { throw ... }` is never registered with PendingErrorRegistry (StoreHandle.kt:314-319 only runs in the handle path), so the headline unconsumed-error safety net silently does not apply to the most natural call shape. `v.suspendAction {}` behaves differently (no member to shadow), making the rules inconsistent per-verb.
allFindings.recommendation: Remove the dead `V.action` extension (it can never win resolution) and give the scope a non-colliding verb that always routes through the handle, e.g. `v.act { }` or `transact(v) { }`; alternatively make `track(v)` the only documented pattern and have the auto-registration KDoc example NOT show `v.action`. At minimum, make the timeline matchers detect an empty timeline + untracked-action situation in their failure message ("timeline is empty — did the action run through Store.action before the store was tracked?").

allFindings.title: suspendAction produces zero timeline events — async tests get empty timelines with no hint why
allFindings.evidence: Recorder.kt:69-72: "**suspendAction** does not run the middleware chain at all ... The recorder therefore sees no events for suspending actions." This is buried in an internal class's KDoc and one clause at StoreHandle.kt:42. A coroutine-first user (the primary KMP audience) writing `v.suspendAction { ... }` then `handle shouldFire { committed }` gets `"shouldFire: 1 predicate(s) did not match any event:\n  - any transaction committed"` (TimelineMatcherRunner.kt:129-139) — the message gives no hint that suspending actions are categorically invisible. `lastResult` and the pending-error guard DO work for suspendAction (StoreHandle.kt:292-297), so the harness behaves half-recorded, which reads as flaky rather than by-design.
allFindings.recommendation: Have `StoreHandle.suspendAction` synthesize TransactionStarted/Committed/Errored events itself (it sees the result and the transaction), clearly flagged, until core 2.0 runs middleware for suspend actions; and/or append a diagnostic line to all four combinator failure messages when the timeline is empty, naming the two known causes (Capture.None, suspendAction v1 contract).

allFindings.title: api() umbrella dependencies: kotest-assertions is api-exposed but never used in code; hallmark pulled in for one matcher
allFindings.evidence: holdfast-testing/build.gradle.kts:25-32 declares `api(project(":holdfast"))`, `api(project(":holdfast-coroutines"))`, `api(project(":holdfast-hallmark"))`, `api("com.vynatix:hallmark:0.1.0")`, `api(libs.kotest.assertions.core)` (kotest 5.9.1 per gradle/libs.versions.toml:15). Zero `io.kotest` imports exist anywhere in holdfast-testing/src — all matchers are hand-rolled AssertionError throwers (ResultMatchers.kt, TimelineMatcherRunner.kt, StateMatchers.kt). Kotest's `shouldBe` appears only in KDoc samples (BridgeView.kt:27-31, RecordingBridge.kt:22-27, OpenTransaction.kt:182-184), blurring which library provides what. The entire hallmark dependency exists for one 27-line matcher (matcher/BoxedMatchers.kt). A consumer who wants only vaultTest + shouldFire gets kotest + hallmark + holdfast-hallmark + coroutines-test on their test classpath unconditionally.
allFindings.recommendation: Drop the kotest api dependency entirely (the harness is self-contained — a genuine strength worth advertising) and rewrite KDoc samples with the harness's own matchers or kotlin.test; move BoxedMatchers into holdfast-hallmark (or a holdfast-hallmark-testing module) so hallmark stops being a transitive tax on non-hallmark users.

allFindings.title: Matcher predicates that v1 can never record produce always-green assertions, and `middleware<M>()` without a property access registers nothing
allFindings.evidence: User-middleware events are never captured in v1 (StoreHandle.kt:240-247, TimelineMatcher.kt:105-108) and bridges attached after track(v) fire no events (StoreHandle.kt:66-72). Combined with the negation combinator this is dangerous: `handle shouldNotFire { middleware<AuditMiddleware>().errored }` or `shouldNotFire { bridgePublished(V::theme) }` (late-attached bridge) passes forever regardless of behavior — a false-green safety assertion. Separately, the register-on-access pattern (TimelineMatcher.kt:33-39, getters at :73-86) means `shouldFire { middleware<MyMw>() }` compiles and registers ZERO predicates (only `.started/.completed/.errored` accesses register, MiddlewareBuilder at :219-237), and the empty-predicate early-return (TimelineMatcherRunner.kt:18,31,58,84) makes it vacuously pass — the user believes they asserted "my middleware ran".
allFindings.recommendation: Make the v1 capture gaps fail loudly: middleware-typed and bridge predicates for never-recordable categories should throw UnsupportedOperationException("user middleware events are not captured in v1") rather than match nothing; make a `middleware<M>()` builder whose scope ends with no property access throw at builder exit; consider failing (or at least warning) on an entirely empty predicate list. The register-on-access getters themselves are fine once seen, but each getter KDoc should lead with "accessing this property registers a predicate".

allFindings.title: No Compose testing story despite shipping a Compose module
allFindings.evidence: holdfast-compose ships `collectAsState`/`rememberDisposable` (ComposeBindings.kt:33-37) but its only test is ComposeBindingsCompileTest.kt (a compile check); holdfast-testing has no Compose artifact, no `runComposeUiTest` interop, and `vaultTest` wraps `runTest` directly (StoreTest.kt:36) so it cannot host a ComposeUiTest scope. Nothing in any doc explains how to verify "commit triggers recomposition". Grep confirms no module in the repo consumes the harness outside holdfast-testing's own tests — the harness is not dogfooded against the Compose or coroutines adapters.
allFindings.recommendation: Add a documented recipe (or a small holdfast-compose-testing artifact) showing `runComposeUiTest { ... }` plus a tracked store: assert recomposition count after `action {}` commit and after rollback. Even a GUIDE.md subsection would close the gap for the most common adopter profile.

allFindings.title: Time-control helpers require the `testScope.` prefix inside vaultTest
allFindings.evidence: StoreTestScope.kt:22-25 and :41-48: the wrapper delegates CoroutineScope and forwards `testScheduler`/`backgroundScope`, but `runCurrent()`, `advanceUntilIdle()`, `advanceTimeBy()`, `currentTime` are TestScope extensions, so inside `vaultTest {}` they don't resolve — users coming from `runTest {}` must discover and write `testScope.advanceUntilIdle()`. The KDoc admits this is a workaround for TestScope being sealed.
allFindings.recommendation: Forward the four common helpers as members on StoreTestScope (`fun runCurrent() = testScope.runCurrent()` etc.) so the muscle memory from runTest carries over verbatim.

allFindings.title: `StoreHandle.bridge()` returns star-projected `BridgeView<*>`, forcing unchecked casts in user assertions
allFindings.evidence: StoreHandle.kt:202 `fun bridge(prop: KProperty1<V, State<*>>): BridgeView<*>`; the harness's own KDoc example must cast: BridgeView.kt:42 `(view.published as List<String>) shouldBe listOf("dark")`.
allFindings.recommendation: Add a typed overload `fun <T : Any> bridge(prop: KProperty1<V, State<T>>): BridgeView<T>` so `view.published` is `List<T>` without casting; keep the star form for heterogeneous walks.

allFindings.title: Throwing action bodies need an explicit type argument: `action<Unit> { throw ... }`
allFindings.evidence: The harness's own tests write `ctr.action<Unit> { throw IllegalStateException("oops") }` everywhere (ResultMatcherTest.kt:140, :154, :170, :178, :195) because the lambda infers `Nothing`. Every user testing the error path — the primary use of the pending-error machinery — hits this papercut on day one.
allFindings.recommendation: Add a dedicated `fun StoreHandle<V>.failingAction(body: V.() -> Any?): TransactionResult.Error` (asserting the result IS an error and returning it typed), which both kills the type argument and pairs naturally with `shouldRollbackWith`.

allFindings.title: AwaitingTimeoutException is a CancellationException subclass — cancellation-tolerant user code can swallow test timeouts
allFindings.evidence: Awaiting.kt:145-147 `class AwaitingTimeoutException internal constructor(message: String) : CancellationException(message)`. The rationale (TCE is final with internal ctor) is honestly documented at :53-61, but common patterns like `catch (e: Exception)`-excluding-CE wrappers, or libraries that treat CancellationException as benign control flow, will silently eat an `awaiting` timeout instead of failing the test.
allFindings.recommendation: Throw a plain AssertionError subclass (matching `eventually`, which throws AssertionError at Eventually.kt:56) unless cooperative-cancellation semantics are specifically needed; if they are, document the swallowing hazard in the `awaiting` KDoc, not just the constructor rationale.

allFindings.title: awaiting timeout message reports the tail size as "saw N events"
allFindings.evidence: Awaiting.kt:125-127: `recent = handles.flatMap { it.timeline }.takeLast(5)` then `"(saw ${recent.size} events: $recent)"` — after 200 events it prints "saw 5 events", understating activity and implying a quiet store.
allFindings.recommendation: Print both: `"saw $total events, last ${recent.size}: $recent"`.

allFindings.title: Capture mode silently ignored when a store is auto-registered before an explicit track(v, Capture.X)
allFindings.evidence: StoreAutoRegistration.kt:44-46 and StoreTestScope.kt:57-59: track is idempotent by identity and "capture on the second call is ignored". A `v.read {}` (or `v.timeline`) anywhere before `track(v, Capture.None)` locks in Capture.All with no warning — order-dependent configuration that fails silently.
allFindings.recommendation: Throw (or at least record a teardown warning) when `track` is called with a capture mode different from the existing handle's, instead of ignoring it.

allFindings.title: Install instructions point to Maven Central, but no com.vynatix artifact exists there
allFindings.evidence: README.md:4 (Maven Central badge), README.md:52-68 (install block: mavenCentral() + implementation("com.vynatix:holdfast:0.1.0")), holdfast/CHANGELOG.md:11-13 ("First public release on Maven Central"). Verified live: https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/com/vynatix/holdfast/maven-metadata.xml returns 404; search.maven.org query g:com.vynatix returns numFound=0. settings.gradle.kts:20 also shows the repo itself relies on mavenLocal() for the sibling com.vynatix:hallmark:0.1.0 dep (holdfast-hallmark/build.gradle.kts:35), which is equally unpublished.
allFindings.recommendation: Either publish 0.1.0 to Central before keeping these claims, or change README to 'not yet published — build from source via publishToMavenLocal' and remove the badge. For holdfast-hallmark, document the two-repo local-publish bootstrap (clone hallmark, publishToMavenLocal, then build holdfast) or vendor a snapshot. The very first copy-paste a prospective adopter performs currently fails, which poisons trust in everything else the docs say.

allFindings.title: README documents a testing entry point `holdfastTest { }` that does not exist — the real function is `vaultTest`
allFindings.evidence: holdfast/README.md:98 and README.md:48 advertise `holdfastTest { }`. Actual public API is `fun vaultTest(...)` (holdfast-testing/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/vynatix/holdfast/testing/StoreTest.kt:32, confirmed sole entry in holdfast-testing/api/holdfast-testing.klib.api:531). The repo's own CLAUDE.md:64 admits: "Entry point is `vaultTest { }` (not `holdfastTest` — stale KDoc mentions it)". Six more KDoc files reference `holdfastTest` (e.g. holdfast-testing/.../matcher/PerformanceMatchers.kt:12, concurrency/Eventually.kt:22).
allFindings.recommendation: Rename `vaultTest` to `storeTest` (matching the Store* class rename) or add a `storeTest` alias, then fix all README/KDoc references. Any newcomer following the README into the testing module hits an unresolved reference on their first test.

allFindings.title: Three brand generations (Vault → Holdfast → Store) leak simultaneously into public API, KDoc samples, and module READMEs
allFindings.evidence: Public API still carries vault names: `EventfulSupport.bindVault` and `MutableState.owningVault` (holdfast/api/holdfast.klib.api:216,225; EventfulSupport.kt:88; MutableState.kt:27). KDoc examples use Vault-era class names: Store.kt:41 (`class CounterVault : Store<CounterVault>`), Effect.kt:19 (`MyVault`), Derived.kt:18 (`CartVault`), EventfulStore.kt:20, ComposeBindings.kt:26,51 (`CounterVault`, `AccountVault`), holdfast-coroutines StateFlows.kt:102 (`MyVault`). Module READMEs use Holdfast-era names: holdfast-coroutines/README.md:36,47 (`CounterHoldfast`, `AccountHoldfast`), holdfast-compose/README.md:23,40, holdfast-hallmark-coroutines/README.md:29 (`UserHoldfast`). GUIDE.md:1331 mixes both in one snippet: `fun AccountStore.transferTo(other: AccountHoldfast, ...)`. Atomic.kt:57 parameter is `vararg vaults`.
allFindings.recommendation: Do one mechanical sweep: rename `bindVault`→`bindStore`, `owningVault`→`owningStore` (pre-1.0 is the only cheap time), regenerate ABI dumps, and normalize every sample class to `*Store`. A newcomer currently has to learn that Vault, Holdfast, and Store all mean the same thing before they can read the KDoc — pure tax with zero payoff.

allFindings.title: Store lifecycle (dispose/scope) and the entire events system are public core API but absent from README and GUIDE
allFindings.evidence: Public surface includes `Store.dispose()`, `isDisposed`, `bindToScope`, `scope`, `Store.defaultScope`, `Eventful<E>`, `EventfulStore`, `EventfulSupport` (holdfast/api/holdfast.klib.api:56-60,120-127,165-187,210-217; Store.kt:83-173). Grep of holdfast/README.md, holdfast/GUIDE.md, and root README.md finds zero mentions of any of these — GUIDE §13's Store member table (GUIDE.md:1013-1024) omits them all. The only documentation lives in the CHANGELOG's 'internal-only history' archive (CHANGELOG.md:49-75) and holdfast-coroutines/2.0-DESIGN.md:83-90. The one ViewModel example (holdfast-coroutines/README.md:35-41) creates a store inside a ViewModel and never disposes it.
allFindings.recommendation: Add a 'Lifecycle' section to the GUIDE answering the questions every ViewModel/MVI migrant asks on day one: who owns the store, who calls dispose() (e.g. ViewModel.onCleared), what `IllegalStateException("store disposed")` means, and when to use bindToScope vs defaultScope. Document EventfulStore as the one-shot UI-events answer (the #1 sidecar feature in MVI libraries — it exists here but is invisible). Right now the most lifecycle-critical API is documented only in an archive explicitly labeled 'not a release log a consumer ever migrated against'.

allFindings.title: README/GUIDE claim 'no coroutines dependency in core' — core has an api() dependency on kotlinx-coroutines-core
allFindings.evidence: holdfast/README.md:12 ("No coroutines dependency in core"), holdfast/README.md:171-172 ("no required dependencies beyond kotlin-stdlib + kotlinx-atomicfu"), GUIDE.md:5-6 ("no coroutine dependency in its API"). Reality: holdfast/build.gradle.kts:49 declares `api(libs.kotlinx.coroutines.core)`; `Eventful.events` exposes `SharedFlow` (api dump line 58), `Store.scope`/`defaultScope` expose `CoroutineScope` (Store.kt:83, api dump 186), Store.kt:689 spins up a Dispatchers.Default scope.
allFindings.recommendation: Fix the claim — say 'kotlin-stdlib + atomicfu + kotlinx-coroutines-core'. Dependency-surface claims are precisely what KMP library evaluators check first; being provably wrong here undermines the (otherwise good) honesty of the positioning section. Alternatively, if coroutine-free core is the actual design goal, move Eventful/scope into :holdfast-coroutines before 1.0.

allFindings.title: GUIDE is organized around internal version numbers (1.0/1.1/2.0/0.3.0) that never shipped, while the published version is 0.1.0
allFindings.evidence: GUIDE.md:29 + 1112-1115 ("## 14. The 1.1 surface — Everything below ships in 1.1 on top of the 1.0 baseline"), GUIDE.md:1290-1297 ("(2.0; was a documented no-op limitation in 1.1)"), GUIDE.md:1363 ("### 14.11 Validation 0.3.0"), Appendix A comments "// 1.1" throughout (GUIDE.md:1647-1688). CHANGELOG.md:17-24 explains these are internal pre-rename vault versions, but GUIDE never says so. A reader installing 0.1.0 cannot map 'ships in 1.1' to anything.
allFindings.recommendation: Strip internal version numbers from the GUIDE entirely — everything in §14 ships in 0.1.0 as far as a consumer is concerned. Rename §14 to 'Extended surface' and delete the '(2.0; ...)' asides or move them to the CHANGELOG archive where the context exists.

allFindings.title: GUIDE §14.11 documents the Hallmark integration under stale module names and dead links
allFindings.evidence: GUIDE.md:1374-1378 lists artifacts `com.vynatix:validation`, `com.vynatix:validation-coroutines`, and module `:validation` — actual modules are `holdfast-hallmark` / `holdfast-hallmark-coroutines` plus the external `com.vynatix:hallmark` repo. GUIDE.md:1539,1606 use headers `holdfast-validation` / `holdfast-validation-coroutines`. GUIDE.md:1635-1637 links `../validation/KONFORM-MIGRATION.md` — path does not exist in this repo. holdfast-hallmark-coroutines/README.md:3 also references `:validation-coroutines`. CHANGELOG.md:38 links `../MIGRATING.md` — also nonexistent.
allFindings.recommendation: Rewrite §14.11 against the shipped names (hallmark repo + holdfast-hallmark adapter), make clear which types live in the external library vs this repo, and remove or restore the KONFORM-MIGRATION.md and MIGRATING.md links. As written, a reader cannot tell what to add to their build file to get `boxed { }`.

allFindings.title: GUIDE contradicts itself and the code about same-value commit deduplication
allFindings.area: doc accuracy / footgun for StateFlow migrants
allFindings.evidence: GUIDE.md:247-249 (§4.4: effect fires "Once per top-level commit that actually changes the raw stored value. (Same-value commits do not re-fire — see §6.)") and GUIDE.md:424,428 (§6 table: "(no fire — dedup)", "Same-value commits are deduped"). But the default is `distinct: Boolean = false` (MutableState.kt:28; dedup gated at MutableState.kt:127 `val same = distinct && currentValue == processedValue`), and GUIDE.md:1015 + §8.4 (GUIDE.md:604-611) correctly describe `distinct=true` as opt-in. StateFlow migrants assume conflation-by-equality is the default; two GUIDE sections confirm that wrong assumption.
allFindings.recommendation: Fix §4.4 and the §6 table to state that same-value commits DO re-fire unless `state(distinct = true)`. Consider flipping the default to `distinct = true` before 1.0 — it matches both StateFlow semantics and what your own docs apparently believe the behavior is.

allFindings.title: Silent-failure defaults: action errors are swallowed into an ignorable result, and observer exceptions vanish by default
allFindings.evidence: GUIDE.md:201-202: action "never throws — exceptions are captured into Error"; `TransactionResult` carries no must-use enforcement, so `store action { ...; error("bug") }` as a statement silently no-ops. Store.kt:213-224: `uncaughtObserverHandler` defaults to null = "exceptions thrown from observer bodies during commit are swallowed silently". Neither README quick start (holdfast/README.md:29-43, which does check the result) nor GUIDE pitfalls (§12) warns about the discard-the-result pattern; uncaughtObserverHandler appears only in the §13 reference table (GUIDE.md:1021).
allFindings.recommendation: Add a prominent footgun callout: 'if you ignore the TransactionResult, failures are invisible — wire LoggingMiddleware or check the result'. Ship a one-liner like `result.getOrThrow()` / `requireSuccess()` for fail-fast call sites, and recommend setting uncaughtObserverHandler in every app's init. Coroutines/StateFlow users come from a world where uncaught exceptions crash loudly; this library inverts that default twice.

allFindings.title: snapshot()/restore() cannot serve the Android process-death use case it implicitly invites, and docs never say so
allFindings.evidence: StoreSnapshot has an internal constructor and internal rawValues with only stateNames/size public (Snapshot.kt:18-26) — values cannot be read out, serialized, or reconstructed, so SavedStateHandle/Parcel persistence is impossible. holdfast/README.md:80 markets "Store.snapshot() / Store.restore()" as a major capability with no scope note; GUIDE.md:1117-1143 and the undo cookbook (GUIDE.md:1345-1350) only show in-memory use. No doc anywhere mentions SavedStateHandle, process death, or ViewModel state restoration (grep across *.md confirms).
allFindings.recommendation: State explicitly that snapshot/restore is in-memory only (undo/redo, test fixtures) and that process-death persistence is KvBridge's job. Better: add a documented recipe mapping store states to SavedStateHandle via KvStore, since that is the first integration question an Android adopter will ask.

allFindings.title: wasmJs support is overstated: tests are disabled and FileSystemKvStore throws at construction, while the headline claims full support
allFindings.evidence: holdfast/README.md:12-13 ("Runs on Android, iOS, JVM, and wasmJs") and README.md:190 ("./gradlew :holdfast:allTests # tests on Android JVM + iOS sim + JVM + wasmJs"). Reality: all wasmJs test tasks are force-disabled (holdfast/build.gradle.kts:60-77, comment: "The test suite uses runBlocking and newSingleThreadContext, neither of which exists on wasmJs"), and `FileSystemKvStore` throws UnsupportedOperationException in its init on wasm (FileSystemKvStore.wasmJs.kt:10-15). The honest caveat exists only in that actual-class KDoc; README:122's '(JVM + iOS)' row is the lone doc hint.
allFindings.recommendation: Change the claim to 'compiles for wasmJs; runtime test coverage currently runs on JVM/Android/iOS' and add a wasm caveats paragraph (no FileSystemKvStore, single-threaded so the concurrency model is vacuous there). Fix the README:190 comment — it asserts test coverage that the build explicitly disables. A wasm adopter today is materially misled.

allFindings.title: No migration story from StateFlow ViewModels or MVI libraries, and no DI guidance
allFindings.evidence: Grep across all *.md: zero mentions of Hilt, Koin, or any migration path. The positioning section (holdfast/README.md:150-174) says when NOT to migrate but never how to migrate. CHANGELOG.md:38 references a MIGRATING.md that doesn't exist (and was vault→holdfast internal anyway). The only ViewModel content is one 7-line snippet (holdfast-coroutines/README.md:32-41). No guidance on store granularity (one per screen? per feature? singleton?), constructor injection, or testing stores behind DI.
allFindings.recommendation: Add a 'Coming from MutableStateFlow' page: side-by-side of a 3-field StateFlow ViewModel rewritten as a Store, including scoping, dispose-in-onCleared, asStateFlow exposure, and a Koin/Hilt module sample. This is the single highest-leverage doc for the stated target audience; today migration cost is unknowable from the docs.

allFindings.title: Positioning never addresses Compose's snapshot system — the closest existing 'transactional state' competitor for the target audience
allFindings.evidence: holdfast/README.md:150-174 compares against StateFlow, Redux/MVI/Mavericks, Molecule, and redux-saga; GUIDE.md §1 table (GUIDE.md:57-66) compares var+listeners, MutableStateFlow, Redux. Neither mentions that Compose's snapshot system (mutableStateOf + Snapshot.withMutableSnapshot) already provides atomic multi-cell writes with isolation — despite shipping a holdfast-compose module that layers the two transactional systems on top of each other (ComposeBindings.kt:33-38).
allFindings.recommendation: Add one positioning bullet: what Holdfast transactions give you that Compose snapshots don't (rollback-on-throw as a contract, middleware, bridges/persistence, non-UI threads, no Compose runtime dependency) and how the two interact in holdfast-compose. Compose-literate reviewers will raise this objection unprompted; pre-empting it builds credibility.

allFindings.title: `by state { }` returns State<T>, not T — inverts the Compose delegate expectation without a doc callout
allFindings.evidence: StateDelegate.getValue returns `State<T>` (Contract.kt:47-52), so `val count by state { 0 }` makes `count: State<Int>` and every read is `count.value`. Compose devs reading `by state { 0 }` pattern-match to `by mutableStateOf(0)` (which yields Int). Neither the README quick start (holdfast/README.md:18-21) nor GUIDE §4.1 (GUIDE.md:167-181) explicitly warns that the delegate yields the wrapper (the `by` exists for property-name capture, not unwrapping).
allFindings.recommendation: Add one explicit line to the quick start: "`count` is a `State<Int>` handle — read with `count.value`, write with `mutate`; unlike Compose's `by mutableStateOf`, the delegate does not unwrap." Cheap fix for the most predictable first-five-minutes confusion.

allFindings.title: holdfast-coroutines README documents a quarter of the module's actual surface
allFindings.evidence: holdfast-coroutines/README.md:6-18 lists only asFlow, asStateFlow(scope), first, awaitValue. The module also ships suspendAction (advertised in root README.md:46 and holdfast/README.md:88), asStateFlow() no-arg overload (StateFlows.kt:116), asEagerStateFlow, suspendAtomic (SuspendAtomic.kt), SuspendingBridge, SuspendingKvStore, InMemorySuspendingKvStore, SuspendingFileSystemKvStore — none in the module README. The wasm FileSystemKvStore KDoc even directs users to SuspendingKvStore (FileSystemKvStore.wasmJs.kt:5-6), which is documented nowhere.
allFindings.recommendation: Regenerate the module README's Surface section from the API dump (holdfast-coroutines/api). suspendAction is arguably the module's headline feature and its own README doesn't mention it.

allFindings.title: GUIDE cookbook contradicts the shipped API: §9.6 claims no derived operator, §9.5/§7.3 teach hand-rolled Compose bridges instead of holdfast-compose
allFindings.evidence: GUIDE.md:739-741: "The library has no native derive(other) { … } operator" — but §14.2 (GUIDE.md:1144-1164) documents `Store.derived(sources)`. GUIDE.md:711-737 (§9.5) hand-rolls a 15-line StateFlowBridge for Compose and §7.3's decision chart (GUIDE.md:530-536) recommends "collectAsState on a StateFlow that you publish from an effect, OR a StateFlow Bridge" — never mentioning holdfast-compose's one-line `collectAsState` documented at §14.9 (GUIDE.md:1302-1315).
allFindings.recommendation: Update §9.6 to lead with `derived(...)` and §9.5/§7.3 to lead with holdfast-compose's collectAsState (keeping the hand-rolled bridge as the 'no compose dependency' fallback). The cookbook reads as pre-1.1 text pasted before the 1.1 section — readers who stop at §9 will hand-build what the library ships.

allFindings.title: Troubleshooting table documents error messages that don't exist in the code
allFindings.evidence: GUIDE.md:1001 documents `IllegalStateException: Failed to record state change` for foreign-state mutation; actual message is "State must be created by this Store instance" (Store.kt:567-568). GUIDE.md:1002 documents `TransactionException: Cannot mutate state on a Committed transaction`; actual is an IllegalStateException from check() (Store.kt:547-549). A user pasting the real exception text into the docs search finds nothing; a user reading the docs searches the codebase for text that isn't there.

A user following 9.8 will expect an unguarded inner failure to abort the outer; instead the outer commits partial state and reports Success — a silent correctness failure, not a cosmetic doc nit. verified.title: Exceptions thrown during commit fanout (transformer.get, Bridge.publish, a throwing uncaughtObserverHandler) produce a PARTIAL commit reported as Error
verified.reasoning:
Every cited evidence point checks out against the code, and the library's own test suite empirically enshrines the partial-commit behavior.

VERIFIED MECHANICS:
1. /Users/osamaraddad/work/extracting/holdfast/holdfast/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/vynatix/holdfast/Transaction.kt:241-243 — top-level commit applies pending writes one by one (`pendingWrites.forEach { (state, value) -> applyTopLevel(state, value) }`), exactly as claimed.
2. MutableState.kt:145-149 — `applyCommitted` first calls `applyCommittedRaw`, which writes `currentValue` under stateLock (lines 126-130) BEFORE running `notifyObservers(afterGet(processedValue))` (line 132, where `afterGet` invokes `transformer.get` unwrapped), then calls `currentBridge?.publish(...)` (line 148, unwrapped). Three unprotected user-code throw points confirmed: transformer.get, bridge.publish, and a throwing `uncaughtObserverHandler` (`handler?.invoke(e)` at MutableState.kt:173 is itself uncaught, even though individual observer throws ARE caught at 168-174 — proving the authors intended fanout to be exception-tolerant but left these gaps).
3. Transaction.kt:273-275 — throw mid-iteration is caught, status → Failed, rethrown as `TransactionException("Commit failed", e)` naming neither the failing state nor the already-applied ones. `pendingWrites.clear()` (line 250) is skipped on throw.
4. Store.kt:386-392 — commit throw caught and returned as `TransactionResult.Error(e, txn)` with no rollback; no undo is even possible — MutableState captures no pre-images (grep for rollback/undo/previousValue in MutableState.kt: zero hits), and Transaction.rollback only clears pending buffers and is a no-op on terminal Failed status.

EMPIRICAL CONFIRMATION FROM THE LIBRARY'S OWN TESTS: `BridgeErrorPathTest.bridgePublishThrowingDoesNotCorruptStateOrLeakActiveTransaction` (holdfast/src/commonTest/.../BridgeTest.kt:281-294) asserts `assertEquals(5, v.count.value, "state mutation completes before publish throws")` after the action returned Error — the new value is retained while the caller holds an Error result. For multi-state actions, states after the failing one in insertion order never apply, giving true partial application.

DOCS CONTRADICTION: README.md:34 states "Failed transactions roll back atomically — observers never fire" — directly false here (status is literally Failed, observers fired, value retained). GUIDE.md:48 says "`action { … }` is atomic; throw rolls back everything" (unqualified). The visibility table (GUIDE.md ~420-424) covers only body-throw and success rows; the commit-fanout-throw case is documented nowhere. Bonus inconsistency: FailingBridge's shipped KDoc usage example (holdfast-testing/.../FailingBridge.kt:20) shows `result shouldRollbackWith ...`, while the actual test (FailingBridgeTest.kt:74-80) had to correct itself to `shouldBeError` because it does NOT roll back — even the maintainers' own docs are confused about this path.

MINOR NITPICK: GUIDE.md:39-41's "all-or-nothing" sentence does scope its elaboration with "if its body throws", so the cleanest contradiction is README.md:34 and GUIDE.md:48, not GUIDE:39-40 alone. This does not weaken the finding.

SEVERITY: major is justified, not exaggerated. Bridge.publish is the documented save-on-commit persistence hook — user I/O code that realistically throws (the maintainers' own test names the cause "kv unreachable"). A caller receiving Error will, per README's promise, assume full rollback and may retry the action (double-applying writes and double-firing observers) or show "nothing saved" UI while in-memory state and observers already advanced. No code mitigation, no doc disclosure, and a generic "Commit failed" message. Not a blocker because: no data is corrupted or lost inside the store, the single-state case is arguably "committed, then notification failed", and the most common fanout user code (observers) is already protected — the window only opens via transformer.get, bridge.publish, or a throwing handler.
verified.evidence: Transaction.kt:241-243 applies pending writes one by one (`pendingWrites.forEach { applyTopLevel(state, value) }`); MutableState.applyCommitted (MutableState.kt:145-149) writes currentValue, then runs afterGet (transformer.get) and `currentBridge?.publish(...)` — both user code that can throw. A throw mid-iteration is caught at Transaction.kt:273-275 → `TransactionException("Commit failed", e)` → Store.kt:390-391 returns TransactionResult.Error. verified.title: emit() checks for an active transaction but not for OWNERSHIP — a racy off-action emit silently stages the event onto another thread's transaction

verified.evidence: EventfulStore.kt:89-96: `val txn = activeTransaction ?: error("emit(event) called outside of an action / suspendAction. Events must be staged inside a transaction so rollback can discard them.")` — when no action is in flight anywhere, this is the best error message in the library. BUT activeTransaction is a volatile cross-thread read (Store.kt:183-193), and unlike mutate (Store.kt:538 checks `txn.ownerThreadId == currentThreadId()`), emit does no ownership check. If thread B calls store.emit(e) (public API via the Eventful interface) while thread A's action is mid-flight, the event is silently staged onto A's transaction (Transaction.kt:112-119 stagePendingEvent just appends under pendingLock) — it then commits or gets discarded with A's unrelated transaction. Same gap in EventfulSupport.kt:104-116. Timing-dependent: the identical call site throws a clean ISE when no action is running and silently misfiles the event when one is — the worst kind of flaky.
verified.recommendation: Mirror mutate's guard in emit: require `txn.ownerThreadId == currentThreadId() || suspendingOwner != null`, else throw the same descriptive 'outside of an action' error. This converts a race-dependent silent misbehavior into the deterministic error users already get in the simple case.
